mainTopic: Burning disqualified קדשים: whose wood and where, the reasons of embarrassment and suspicion, and the sources for burning a פסח that went out or became טמא
overview: This amud covers how and why disqualified קדשים are burned. It opens by resolving a contradiction about whether disqualified meat is burned at home with one's own wood or in front of the בירה with עצי המערכה. רב חמא בר עוקבא splits the cases into a visitor (אכסנאי) and a resident (בעל הבית). רב פפא says both cases are about a visitor and asks whether he has already set out on the road. רב זביד defends the first split: since a visitor has no wood of his own, the חכמים treated him like the ציקנין. A ברייתא then forbids mixing place and wood. רב יוסף explains the ban on bringing your own wood to the בירה as protecting the poor from embarrassment, and רבא explains it as preventing suspicion of theft. The same two אמוראים give the same two reasons for why impure כהנים stood at the eastern gate. A new משנה follows: a פסח that went out or became טמא is burned right away, but if its owners became טמא or died it waits for עיבור צורה, and רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה disagrees. The גמרא derives the burning of יוצא from משה's conversation with אהרן, then challenges whether that source reaches קדשים קלים like the פסח. It begins a second challenge about blood left overnight, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The contradicting source: burn it before the Temple with altar wood
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of a contradiction. The other source says disqualified meat is burned in front of the בירה with עצי המערכה. That clashes with our משנה, which says to burn it at home with one's own wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The other source says:] He goes back and burns it in front of the Temple, using wood from the altar pile!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a source that seems to contradict our משנה. That source says to burn the meat in front of the Temple with altar wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says people burn disqualified meat in their own courtyards or on their roofs with their own wood. This source says the meat goes back to the Temple and is burned with עצי המערכה, which is holy wood. So which is it: your own wood at home, or Temple wood at the Temple?

keyTerms.meaning: Wood from the altar pile, which belongs to the Temple
He goes back and burns it

steps.confusionAlert: This line is only the last part of a contradiction. The opening words that introduced it (the other source) came on the previous amud. The point is the clash with our משנה's rule of burning at home with one's own wood.

phrases.english: he goes back and burns it in front of the Temple
phrases.notes: This is the last line of the source that seems to contradict ours.

phrases.english: from the wood of the altar pile!
phrases.notes: That's the problem: our משנה says he burns it with his own wood at home.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹזֵר וְשׂוֹרְפוֹ לִפְנֵי הַבִּירָה מֵעֲצֵי הַמַּעֲרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contradiction (רמינהו) that began on the previous amud
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה's rule that disqualified meat is burned at home with one's own wood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another source says it is burned at the Temple with altar wood. The two rules seem to directly conflict.

steps.title: Visitor versus resident
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא בר עוקבא answers that the sources speak about different people. A visitor uses Temple wood, and a resident uses his own wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא בר עוקבא said: It is not difficult. Here, it is talking about a visitor. There, it is talking about a resident.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חמא בר עוקבא solves the contradiction by saying each source is about a different kind of person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source that uses עצי המערכה is about an אכסנאי, a visitor to ירושלים who has no wood there. Our משנה, which requires one's own wood, is about a בעל הבית who lives in ירושלים and has his own wood. Both rules are true, each for a different person.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the standard opening of an answer
A visitor or guest staying in ירושלים
Here ... there; used to split two sources into two cases

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר עוּקְבָא: לָא קַשְׁיָא,
phrases.english: Rav Chama bar Ukva said: It is not difficult;
here, it is about a visitor,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the source that says to use the altar wood.

phrases.english: there, it is about a resident.
phrases.notes: "There" means our משנה, which says to use your own wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר עוּקְבָא: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source applies to a different person
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources give conflicting rules for the same situation
steps.terutzMaskana: A visitor uses altar wood. A resident uses his own wood.

steps.title: Both are visitors: has he set out on the road or not?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a different answer. Both sources are about a visitor. The difference is whether he has already started his journey home.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Both this and that are about a visitor. Here, he has already set out on the road. There, he has not yet set out on the road.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a second way to solve the contradiction. He divides the cases in a different place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא says both sources deal with an אכסנאי. If the visitor has already set out on the road (החזיק בדרך), it is hard for him to gather wood, so he may use עצי המערכה. If he has not yet left, he can still gather his own wood, so he must use it. In this view, a visitor does not automatically get to use Temple wood.

keyTerms.meaning: He has set out on the road (begun his journey)

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: הָא וְהָא בְּאַכְסְנַאי,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: This and that are both about a visitor;
here, where he has already set out on the road,
phrases.notes: So he may use altar wood

phrases.english: there, where he has not set out on the road.
phrases.notes: So he must use his own wood

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: הָא וְהָא בְּאַכְסְנַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to step 1 that disagrees with step 2's split
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different case split: whether the visitor has started his journey
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being a visitor alone is enough to permit altar wood (step 2)
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a visitor who has already set out on the road may use altar wood

steps.title: Back to the first answer: a visitor is treated like the misers
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד upholds רב חמא בר עוקבא's visitor/resident split. Even a visitor who has not left yet may use altar wood, because the חכמים treated him like the ציקנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: Really, it is as was said at first: here it is about a visitor, there about a resident. And even though he has not set out on the road, a visitor, since he has no wood, was treated by the חכמים like the misers.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד rejects רב פפא's distinction and goes back to the first answer. He adds a reason why every visitor may use the Temple wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא needed the visitor to be on the road. רב זביד says that detail does not matter. Since an אכסנאי has no wood of his own, the חכמים gave him the same status as the ציקנין, who are allowed to use עצי המערכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually; used to return to an earlier position

steps.confusionAlert: רב זביד is not giving a brand-new split. He is defending the first answer (visitor/resident) and explaining why it works even for a visitor who has not yet left.

phrases.aramaic: רַב זְבִיד אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם כִּדְאָמַר מֵעִיקָּרָא —
phrases.english: Rav Zevid said: Really, it is as was said at first:
here about a visitor, there about a resident;

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא הֶחְזִיק בַּדֶּרֶךְ,
phrases.english: and even though he has not set out on the road,
phrases.notes: This pushes back on רב פפא's condition about setting out on the road.

phrases.english: a visitor, since he does not have [his own wood],
they made him like the misers.
phrases.notes: The חכמים gave him the misers' status

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב זְבִיד אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם כִּדְאָמַר מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 3 and returns to step 2, adding a reason
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defends the first split and supplies its legal basis
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A visitor may use altar wood only once he is on the road (רב פפא)
steps.terutzMaskana: Every visitor may use altar wood, because he is treated like the ציקנין
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the visitor's permission does not come from how hard his situation is. It comes from a legal category the חכמים created: he is treated like the ציקנין.

steps.title: Source: the misers may burn it with altar wood
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד brings our משנה as the source. It says the ציקנין burn the meat in front of the בירה so they can use עצי המערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in the משנה: The misers burn it in front of the Temple in order to benefit from the wood of the altar pile.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד quotes a משנה to show that the 'misers' category exists and that it permits using the Temple wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה itself says the ציקנין may burn disqualified meat at the Temple and use עצי המערכה. Since the visitor was placed in this same category, he too may use the altar wood. This closes the contradiction.
steps.whatToRemember: A resident burns disqualified meat at home with his own wood. A visitor, like the ציקנין, may burn it at the Temple with עצי המערכה. רב פפא disagrees and allows this only for a visitor who has already set out on the road.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: הַצִּיקָנִין שׂוֹרְפִין אוֹתוֹ לִפְנֵי הַבִּירָה
phrases.english: As we learned: The misers burn it in front of the Temple
in order to benefit from the wood of the altar pile.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הַצִּיקָנִין שׂוֹרְפִין אוֹתוֹ לִפְנֵי הַבִּירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for step 4's comparison to the ציקנין
steps.raayaObject: That the ציקנין category permits using altar wood, which the visitor shares
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה: הציקנין שורפין אותו לפני הבירה בשביל ליהנות מעצי המערכה

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids mixing location and wood
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that you cannot burn at home with Temple wood, and you cannot burn in front of the בירה with your own wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If people came to burn it in their courtyards using wood from the altar pile, we do not listen to them. If they wanted to burn it in front of the בירה using their own wood, we do not listen to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that pairs each place with one kind of wood: home goes with your own wood, and the בירה goes with Temple wood. You cannot mix and match. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the sources linked each place with its own kind of wood. This ברייתא makes the link strict in both directions. Each of the two mixed combinations is forbidden, and this sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: we do not listen to them; the request is refused

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If they came to burn it in their courtyards
and with wood from the altar pile —
we do not listen to them.
In front of the בירה with their own wood —
we do not listen to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא confirming the strict pairing of place and wood that underlies the earlier answers.
steps.raayaObject: That place and wood type must match: home with private wood, בירה with altar wood
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burning at home with altar wood is refused, and burning in front of the בירה with one's own wood is also refused.

steps.title: Why can't private wood be used at the בירה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands the first rule because leftover sacred wood might be misused. It asks for the reason behind the second rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that we refuse people who want to use altar wood in their courtyards, because they might leave some over and come to a mishap with it. But in front of the בירה with their own wood, why not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of the ברייתא. Then it asks what is wrong with the second half. This question sets up the two answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking altar wood home risks leftover sacred wood being used for ordinary purposes. That would be מעילה, a misuse of הקדש. Bringing your own wood to the Temple has no such risk, so the ban needs a different explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: a mishap; here, misuse of sacred property

phrases.english: It makes sense that with altar wood in their courtyards
we do not listen to them —
perhaps some of it will be left over,
and they will come to a mishap with it.
But in front of the בירה with their own wood,
what is the reason it is not allowed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the second half of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for banning private wood in front of the בירה

steps.title: Two reasons: embarrassment or suspicion
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the rule prevents embarrassing the poor. רבא says it prevents suspicion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: So as not to embarrass someone who does not have wood. רבא said: Because of suspicion.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different reasons for the ban on bringing your own wood to the בירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף: if the wealthy brought their own wood, the people using altar wood would be marked as poor. רבא: someone carrying his leftover wood home from the Temple might be suspected of stealing sacred wood.

keyTerms.meaning: one who does not have (the poor)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לְבַיֵּישׁ אֶת מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ.
phrases.english: So as not to embarrass one who does not have.
Rava said:
Because of suspicion.
phrases.notes: Suspicion of stealing sacred wood when taking leftovers home.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: שֶׁלֹּא לְבַיֵּישׁ אֶת מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יוסף: to avoid shaming the poor. רבא: to avoid suspicion of theft from הקדש.

steps.title: The practical difference: reeds and palm branches
steps.stepSummary: The two reasons give different results when someone brings reeds or palm branches, which are never used on the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them? The difference is when someone brings reeds or palm branches, which are not fit for the altar pile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two reasons ever lead to different rulings, and it names a case where they do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reeds and palm branches are never used on the altar. So nobody would suspect a person carrying them home of stealing Temple wood, and רבא's concern does not apply. רב יוסף's concern still applies, because the poor would still stand out. רבא would permit it, and רב יוסף would forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?
the wood pile on the altar

steps.whatToRemember: Home means your own wood, and the בירה means altar wood. No mixing is allowed. רב יוסף bans private wood at the בירה to protect the poor, and רבא bans it to prevent suspicion. They disagree about reeds and palm branches: רבא permits them, and רב יוסף forbids them.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not disagree with the ברייתא. Both אמוראים forbid ordinary private wood. They only differ about wood that is unfit for the altar.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
The difference between them is
where he brought reeds and palm branches,
which are not fit for the altar pile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a case where the two reasons from step 8 lead to different rulings.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For wood unfit for the altar, רבא permits bringing it to the בירה and רב יוסף forbids it.

steps.title: A משנה in תמיד about impure priests at the eastern gate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת תמיד. It says the head of the watch made the impure כהנים stand at the eastern gate.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: the head of the watch would make the impure כהנים stand at the eastern gate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source that sets up the next move. It will show that רב יוסף and רבא argue here in the same way they argued about burning in front of the בירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a different case, but it has the same shape as the last discussion. People are made to do something in public, and we need to know why. The גמרא is preparing to ask about the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The head of the watch (the group of כהנים serving that week)
The eastern gate of the Temple courtyard

phrases.english: We learned there (in a משנה elsewhere):
The head of the watch would stand
the impure (priests) at the eastern gate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel case where the same two אמוראים give the same two kinds of reasons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impure כהנים were made to stand at the eastern gate.

steps.title: Why make them stand at the gate?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind making the impure כהנים stand at the gate.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the impure כהנים had to stand at the gate instead of simply going home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impure כהנים cannot serve anyway, so standing them in public needs an explanation. The question opens the way for the two reasons that follow.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Why not just send them home?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule quoted in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of making impure כהנים stand at the eastern gate.

steps.title: Embarrassment or suspicion
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says it is to embarrass them. רבא says it is to avoid suspicion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: it is to embarrass them. רבא said: it is because of suspicion.
steps.whatsHappening: Two answers are given, and they match the two reasons from before. רב יוסף says shame, and רבא says preventing suspicion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף: they are shamed in public so they will be more careful not to become טמא. רבא: they stand in public so everyone sees they are absent because they are טמא, and nobody thinks they skipped the עבודה to go to work.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of suspicion, so people will not suspect them

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: in order to embarrass them.
phrases.notes: They were not careful to stay pure.

phrases.english: Rava said: because of suspicion.
phrases.notes: So no one thinks they skipped the service to go to work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יוסף: to embarrass them; רבא: to avoid suspicion.

steps.title: What is the practical difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in which case the two reasons would lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks when it would actually matter which reason is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In most cases both reasons lead to the same rule: stand at the gate. The גמרא looks for a case where one reason applies and the other does not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is (the difference) between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical difference between the two answers in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two reasons lead to different rules.

steps.title: Pampered people or rope-twisters
steps.stepSummary: The difference is people who never work, or people who do lowly rope-twisting work. No one would suspect them, so רבא's reason does not apply, but רב יוסף's does.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is pampered people. Or else, someone who twists ropes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two cases where the reasons split. In these cases suspicion is not a worry, but embarrassment still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pampered person never works, so nobody would think he skipped the עבודה to earn money. A rope-twister's job is so lowly and pays so little that nobody would think he skipped the עבודה for it. Under רבא these people do not need to stand at the gate. Under רב יוסף they still must stand there, to be embarrassed.

keyTerms.meaning: Pampered, delicate people who do not work

steps.whatToRemember: Both here and in front of the בירה, רב יוסף's reason is shame and רבא's reason is suspicion. The practical difference is always a case where no one would be suspected.

phrases.english: There is (a difference) between them: pampered people,
phrases.notes: They never work, so no one would suspect them.

phrases.english: or alternatively, one who twists ropes.
phrases.notes: No one skips the עבודה for such low-paying work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 and closes this parallel discussion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Pampered people or rope-twisters: no suspicion, so only רב יוסף requires them to stand at the gate.

steps.title: New משנה: when a פסח is burned right away and when it must wait
steps.stepSummary: A פסח that went out or became טמא is burned right away. If the owners became טמא or died, the meat waits for עיבור צורה and is burned on the sixteenth.
steps.simpleTranslation: A פסח that went out or became impure is burned right away. If the owners became impure or died, its form must change, and it is burned on the sixteenth.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sorts invalid פסח meat into two groups: meat that is burned at once, and meat that must wait first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the meat itself is ruined, because it went out of its area or became טמא, it is burned right away. When the meat is fine but the owners cannot eat it, it must wait until it becomes נותר through עיבור צורה. The fifteenth is יום טוב, and קדשים are not burned on יום טוב, so it is burned on the sixteenth.

keyTerms.meaning: Went out of the area where it may be eaten
Its form must 'pass,' meaning it is left overnight until it becomes נוֹתָר

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the owners' case is less serious, or that the meat is not פסול. The meat is פסול in both cases. The difference is only how it is burned: if the meat itself has a flaw it is burned now, and if the flaw is with the owners it must wait for עיבור צורה.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A Paschal lamb that went out or that became impure —
should be burned immediately.
If the owners became impure or died —
its form must decay (be left overnight),
and it should be burned on the sixteenth.
phrases.notes: Not on the fifteenth, because it is יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is connected by the theme of burning פסולי פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat that went out or became טמא is burned immediately. If the owners became טמא or died, it waits for עיבור צורה and is burned on the 16th.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה: the owners' case is also burned right away
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says that even when the owners became טמא or died, the פסח is burned right away, because no one can eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says: this one too is burned right away, since it has no one to eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the משנה disagrees about the owners' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, having no one who can eat the meat is just as final as a flaw in the meat itself. So there is no reason to wait for עיבור צורה.

keyTerms.meaning: It has no one to eat it

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says:
This too should be burned immediately
because it has no one to eat it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion's rule for the owners' case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when the owners became טמא or died, the פסח is burned immediately.

steps.title: Where do we learn that meat that went out must be burned?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that impure meat is burned, because a פסוק says so. It asks for the source that meat that went out (יוצא) is also burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for impure meat, since it is written: 'The meat that touches anything impure shall not be eaten; it shall be burned in fire.' But meat that went out, where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by asking for a source. It is setting up the next step, which will give the source for burning יוצא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats יוצא and טמא the same way: burn right away. The תורה clearly says impure meat is burned (ויקרא ז:יט). No פסוק here says that meat that left its area is burned, so the גמרא asks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable (we accept this part)
It shall be burned in fire
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: GEMARA: Granted, impure (meat): it is written:
"And the meat that touches anything impure
shall not be eaten; it shall be burned in fire."
But (meat that) went out, from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה of step 15 by asking for a source for one of its rulings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A Torah source that meat which went outside its permitted area must be burned.

steps.title: משה questions אהרן about the uneaten חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a פסוק and retells the conversation between משה and אהרן. משה checks whether the חטאת had a problem that required burning: blood brought inside, or meat taken outside its area. אהרן says neither happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "Behold, its blood was not brought into the Sanctuary within." משה said to אהרן: Why didn't you eat the חטאת? Maybe its blood went into the innermost area? אהרן said: No. משה said: Maybe it went outside its boundary? אהרן said: No, it stayed in the holy area. משה said: If it stayed in the holy area, and its blood was not brought inside, why didn't you eat it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering the question from step 17 by quoting a פסוק and explaining it as a conversation between משה and אהרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה asks about two possible problems that would have made the חטאת unfit to eat. The first is blood brought into the inner Sanctuary. The second is meat taken outside its boundary. משה's questions only make sense if each of these problems would have been a good reason not to eat the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin-offering (here, the offering brought on the eighth day of the משכן's inauguration)
The innermost area of the Sanctuary
Boundary or partition: the area where the meat is allowed to be
The holy area (here, the courtyard where the meat belongs)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two places called "קודש" here. In the פסוק, "הקודש פנימה" means the inner Sanctuary, where the blood should NOT go. In אהרן's answer, "בקודש היתה" means the courtyard, where the meat SHOULD stay.

phrases.english: As it is written: "Behold, its blood was not brought
into the Sanctuary within."
Moshe said to Aharon:
Why didn't you eat the sin-offering?
Perhaps its blood entered the innermost area?
He said to him: No.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: שֶׁמָּא חוּץ לִמְחִיצָתָהּ יָצְתָה?
phrases.english: He said to him: Perhaps it went out beyond its boundary?
He said to him: No, it was in the holy area.
He said to him: If it was in the holy area,

phrases.aramaic: וְ״הֵן לֹא הוּבָא אֶת דָּמָהּ אֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ פְּנִימָה״,
phrases.english: and "behold, its blood was not brought into the Sanctuary within,"
why didn't you eat it?

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: הֵן לֹא הוּבָא אֶת דָּמָהּ אֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ פְּנִימָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 about the source for burning יוצא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the conversation between משה and אהרן, based on ויקרא י:יח.

steps.title: Inference: meat that left its area must be burned
steps.stepSummary: From משה's questions, the גמרא infers that meat which left its boundary, or whose blood entered inside, must be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: This proves that if it goes out, or if its blood goes inside, it is meant to be burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from the conversation: יוצא is a reason for burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה complained only because neither problem had happened. That shows that if either problem had happened, burning would have been correct. So יוצא now has a source.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit for burning; it must be burned

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the Torah source for the rule in the משנה that a פסח which went out is burned. The next step tests how far this source reaches.

phrases.english: This implies that if it went out,
or also if its blood entered inside —
it must be burned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the legal conclusion from the dialogue in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: Sacrificial meat that is יוצא must be burned.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משה's questions to אהרן about the חטאת.

steps.title: The source covers only most-holy offerings, not lesser ones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the source. The rule for impure meat was taught about קדשים קלים, so it applies even more to קדשי קדשים. But the rule for יוצא was learned from a חטאת, which is קדשי קדשים. So how do we know it applies to קדשים קלים, like the פסח?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for meat that became impure: the Torah revealed that rule for offerings of lesser holiness, so it is all the more true for the most holy offerings. But for meat that went out, we found a source only for the most holy offerings. For offerings of lesser holiness, how do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that the new source does not cover the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule taught about a lower level of holiness also applies to a higher level (כל שכן). The opposite does not follow. The חטאת was קדשי קדשים, so the lesson from it may not extend to קדשים קלים. The פסח is קדשים קלים, so its rule of burning when יוצא still lacks a source.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (opens a contrast that leads to a challenge)
Offerings of lesser holiness (for example, שלמים and the פסח)
Offerings of the highest holiness (for example, חטאת)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the rule works in both directions. Lesser holiness to greater holiness works (כל שכן). Greater holiness to lesser holiness does not automatically work.

phrases.english: It makes sense regarding meat that became impure:
the Merciful One revealed it regarding offerings of lesser holiness,
so all the more so regarding the most holy offerings.
But regarding meat that went out, we found it for the most holy offerings;
for offerings of lesser holiness, from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא נִטְמָא, גַּלִּי רַחֲמָנָא בְּקָדָשִׁים קַלִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the source in step 19 reaches the פסח.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation of יוצא from the חטאת of משה and אהרן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חטאת is קדשי קדשים. A rule learned from a higher level of holiness cannot automatically be applied to a lower level, so קדשים קלים such as the פסח are not covered.

steps.title: A second challenge begins: blood left overnight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a further difficulty, starting to quote a ברייתא about an offering whose blood was left overnight. The challenge continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, regarding what was taught in a ברייתא: if its blood was left overnight,
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא to build a second challenge, which is completed on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ותו ("and furthermore") signals that another source problem is coming, on top of the one in step 20. Here the ברייתא's case, blood left overnight, is only introduced.

phrases.english: And furthermore, that which was taught in a baraita:
if its blood was left overnight,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge alongside step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The source for the ruling in a ברייתא about blood left overnight (completed on the next amud).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. The ברייתא is being introduced to show another case whose source still needs explaining.
